messages:
Maya Chen: Customer acme-marketing (acct=acme-789) reporting a sudden p99 spike + 503s starting ~03:10 UTC. They are pinned to eu-central-1 but a lot of traffic is being routed to us-west-2 during the window. They see large queuing then fallback; sample request_ids: req-19321-a1, req-19321-a2. Customer also flagged unexpected cross-region billing. Can we triage?

Raj Patel: Can you paste one of the failing requests (headers + small payload) and any router logs you have? Also: are they pinned with fallbacks disabled?

Maya Chen: here's the minimal repro they shared (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx" 
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-central-1" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"test","request_id":"req-19321-a1"}'
```
They confirm their project config shows: `pinned_region: eu-central-1` and `allow_fallback: true` (they thought fallback was false, so possible config mismatch).

Lila Gómez: pulled router audit logs for that window. Note snippets: 
```
[2026-03-10T03:11:05Z] route decision: project=acme-789 src=api-gw-eu -> target=eu-central-1 (ok)
[2026-03-10T03:11:05Z] target overload: eu-central-1 queue_len=462 active_shards=10 reason=hot_shard_capacity
[2026-03-10T03:11:05Z] fallback applied: eu-central-1 -> us-west-2 (policy=auto-spill, reason=queue_exceeded)
[2026-03-10T03:11:06Z] request req-19321-a1 lat=2100ms status=200 target=us-west-2
```
So the router is honoring `allow_fallback:true` and using the auto-spill policy when the queue length crosses the threshold.

Jonah Park: quick questions: did the autoscaler trigger for eu-central-1? If autoscale lagged, queueing can trigger spillover. Also re: billing — cross-region serves will incur egress.

Maya Chen: autoscaler logs show scaling started at 03:11:20 but the queue threshold is 300 and we hit ~460 before new capacity came up. Autoscale policy is conservative for this cluster (scale step=1).

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-08.14 included autoscaler tuning and a sticky-routing tweak (sticky_ttl=30s). No change to spillover threshold.

Raj Patel: steps to reproduce locally (recommended):
1) Start a stress run targeting eu-central-1 backend group with short seq lengths.
2) Use this python loop to simulate many concurrent short requests.

```python
import requests, threading
for i in range(1000):
    threading.Thread(target=lambda: requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-test','X-Client-Region':'eu-central-1'}, json={'model':'rwd-3b','input':'hi','request_id':f'req-{i}'})).start()
```
This will recreate queue pressure and cause router to evaluate spillover rules.

Lila Gómez: observed behavior summary: when queue_len > queue_threshold (300) router marks target overloaded and uses `auto-spill` which currently allows cross-region fallback even for pinned projects that have `allow_fallback:true`. We need to verify the precedence: pinned_region + allow_fallback=false should block spillover.

Maya Chen: confirming customer believed they had `allow_fallback:false`. They were on a workspace template that sets `allow_fallback:true` by default — docs mismatch. Customer accepted temporary fix to set an explicit project override to `allow_fallback:false` and we applied an emergency rate-limit proxy at the edge to keep requests queued instead of routing cross-region.

billing-bot: Customer noted a spike in cross-region egress charges; flagged for potential credit review. Customer requested documentation on fallback billing behavior.

Jonah Park: Mitigations:
- Short-term: keep explicit `allow_fallback:false` on customer's project (done) and edge rate-limit to avoid spillover.
- Mid-term: change router precedence so `pinned_region + allow_fallback:false` prevents any cross-region fallback when queueing starts (unless explicit admin override).
- Long-term: adjust autoscaler aggressiveness or pre-warm capacity for customers with strict region pinning.

Raj Patel: I'll create a reproducible test case for eng-runtime and tag @eng-runtime. Please include the small load script and router logs.

Maya Chen: Customer accepted the temporary mitigation and asked for ETA on a permanent fix. I'll loop them in once we have a schedule.

Jonah Park: Filing follow-up ticket: https://go/internal/incidents/INC-2026-0345 (assigning to eng-runtime, priority P2). Please add root cause investigation notes and proposed config change. :eyes: 

Lila Gómez: also adding a docs PR to make default fallback behavior explicit for workspace templates.

Maya Chen: thanks — tagging @oncall to keep watch for any more spillover windows this week.

Jonah Park: noted. Closing this slack thread; follow-ups will happen in INC-2026-0345 and a PR thread.
